- Complete pith disintegration — only fibrous vascular bundles remain
- Light gray/white/tan color throughout
- Very dry, shredded appearance
- No wet rot, no obvious colored mycelium

This points to a stalk rot disease. Top candidates: **Charcoal_stalk_rot** (gray-black sclerotia, shredded pith), **Diplodia_stalk_rot** (white bleached pith, shredded), or **Fusarium** (pink tinge).

- **Diplodia**: Shows external stalk views, not internal shredded pith pattern
- **Anthracnose_stalk_rot**: Shows dark/black external lesions, different presentation
- **Physoderma_stalk_rot**: Shows dark purple/brown wet rot at base

The match to Charcoal_stalk_rot is definitive — the reference image contains a near-identical specimen on the same blue background.
